content:
Mulcair should stay as our leader because voters have now become familiar with him (and the party) - respect him, and see him as an instant alternative to Justin Trudeau. Changing would mean starting from scratch - being forgotten - losing the trust.
I've struggled with this a lot and I've decided I want him to continue. I'm looking at it from a business background. First of all, we need to see the failure in the last election as extremely good exposure. When we do that, we realize this is the first time the entire country was looking into the NDP as a viable option. AKA Lots of research and consideration.

Thomas went for a reserved plan, and, he did lose for it (among other things like focusing too much on Quebec, losing it in the end anyways). But that doesn't mean Thomas Mulcair failed the party for long term success. If we consider the fact this was the first time most people ever met Mulcair as well, and also the first time a lot of people considered the NDP, we start to see that people have now familiarized themselves with the party regardless of the loss. Exposure and familiarity are great things, even in a loss. People see Mulcair as a responsible, respectful person who stands up for what he believes and doesn't have crazy off the chart ideas.

They perceive the NDP as a trustworthy party now and they know the leader! Both are living room names are are respected. They see him as an instant possible alternative to Justin Trudeau should things go sour. More importantly, they know he exists unlike whoever picks up the torch next.

We need to keep Mulcair because average voters (not people who pay attention consistently like us) know who he is now. Changing would mean starting from scratch again - going back to old ways - being forgotten. Let voters take a second look, or a third look (incase Trudeau wins a second term). Mulcair is the right guy for the NDP during its first generation in the limelight. 

Telling a man he failed on his first try does not give credit for what he learns after.
